decisions: TPAP with a LAT: order [SHA256_HEX_UPPER(LAT), best password variant] (sha256 if extra_crypt else md5); MAX_ATTEMPTS=2 and the auth breaker are unchanged. Without a LAT the order and messages are unchanged. Extra_crypt shaping applies to the LAT passcode too (same as password candidates).

v3 secure login: device_confirm is checked locally against the LAT and the password (no attempt spent); the matching secret drives keys, digest_passwd and tapo_tag. Legacy MD5 login unchanged (spec only covers encrypt_type 3).
:8800: when a LAT exists it is the digest and stream-key secret (transform gives SHA256_HEX_UPPER(LAT) for encrypt_type 3); the cloud password only when no LAT.

IoT /v2/things is unsigned; HTTP 401 or -20651/-20652/-20675 -> one silent re-login (cached IoT URL dropped). With an https bootstrap URL, a non-https IoT URL is refused so the token is never sent in clear.
Token map keyed by thingName (and deviceId if present); thingName == cloud deviceId assumed (spec unresolved item).

AccountManager: fetch failure or a client without the API -> tokens unknown -> stored LATs kept; a successful fetch without a token for a camera removes its LAT. Vault changes go through AppController.upsert_cameras(local_tokens=...), which restarts only cameras whose LAT changed.

TapoCameraService re-reads the vault LAT on each control call and rebuilds the client (new breaker) when it changed; start_stream replaces a running local supervisor whose LAT differs. LAT kwargs are passed only when a LAT exists so older factories keep working.
Diagnostics: TapoCameraService.diagnostics(), connect() auth errors and the camera-list tooltip say only 'using local access token: yes/no'.
open_issues: Not verified against the real cloud/cameras (by instruction). thingName == deviceId and the exact IoT error body for an expired token are assumptions from the spec.

If the cloud returns no LAT and both password candidates fail, the camera holds an older LAT/password; only the owner can reset it via changeAdminPassword over the cloud passthrough (lat.sync.*), not implemented (needs explicit user consent).
LAT is re-fetched on sign-in/restore/refresh only; no 24 h timer or automatic re-fetch after a TPAP -40401.
